_comment: ADR-0109 lifecycle-status gate policy. ONE required lane over EVERY config in configs_dir, replacing the nine tools/oya-governance-*-lifecycle-app dev-CLI crates that were never referenced by .github/workflows/** and therefore enforced nothing for their entire lifetime. Adding a lifecycle is a CONFIG file here, never a new crate; the completeness dimension makes an unevaluated config fail closed, so a lane cannot be born dark the way the nine dev-CLIs were. MEASURED on the live corpus at first wiring: only 2 of the 9 declared lifecycles observed anything at all. THAT IS NO LONGER TRUE, and the difference is a ruling per lane rather than a new mechanism. The seven dark lanes each took a re-root-or-delete disposition: six configs whose declared corpus does not exist on disk were DELETED, and api-stability-tier was RE-ROOTED onto registry/catalog/*.yaml. 3 configs remain and ALL 3 observe a live corpus — measured by the gate itself at this tree: adr-status 10 artifacts, api-stability-tier 750, doc-status 2702. known_broken_lanes is now EMPTY, and that is the load-bearing consequence: an entry there is the only thing that suppresses lifecycle_status_lane_discovery_failed and lifecycle_status_lane_discovered_nothing, so with nothing listed every lane's anti-vacuity floor is ARMED. A future move that walks a scan root out from under a lane now REDS this required context instead of observing zero and reporting a clean green — which is precisely how these seven went dark in the first place.
purpose: ADR-0109 lifecycle state-machine ratchet: every declared lifecycle config is evaluated against the live corpus, per (lane, violation_kind) counts are frozen shrink-only, and a lane that cannot see its corpus is blocking rather than vacuously green.

frozen_violation_baseline._comment: FROZEN shrink-only per (lane, violation_kind) counts, MEASURED against the live corpus. An absent pair is born-blocking; growth is a regression; a count that FALLS makes this baseline stale and must shrink in the same reviewed PR, so a fixed violation cannot leave headroom for the next one. EVERY config on disk is now a lane that observes a live corpus, so the earlier note that only two of nine appeared here is retired: there is no unbaselined-because-unobservable tier left, and known_broken_lanes is empty. A lane with NO row here is not exempt — it is asserting zero violations of every kind, since an absent (lane, kind) pair is born-blocking.

adr-status-lifecycle._comment: Live apex ADRs only (docs/decisions/ADR-*.md post-disposition). All carry readable status scalars; historical corpus is under docs/adr-archive/ outside this source glob. Zero-count pairs omitted (absent pair is already born-blocking). Measured 2026-08-06 PR #1574. NOTE the consequence of a clean lane: with no violation row, this lane's ONLY floor is `artifacts > 0` via LaneDiscoveredNothing, which is weaker than a shrink-only count. That is accepted here because the corpus is 10 apex records and any drop to zero is a scan-root move, not a slow drift.

api-stability-tier-lifecycle._comment: NO VIOLATION ROW, and the absence is a measured ruling rather than an omission. Measured at HEAD by the gate itself: 750 registry/catalog/*.yaml observed, ZERO violations, after the config's stage vocabulary was aligned to the repo's canonical [preview, stable, GA] tiers. An earlier draft of this block froze `unknown_stage: 750`; that was WRONG twice over and is recorded here because the rule generalises. First, a 100% failure rate on a SINGLE violation code is a config-mismatch signature, not a debt signature — sample the declared values before proposing any baseline. Second, the only remedy for that frozen count was declaring higher tiers per crate, which marketplace/facade/dev-cli/src/governance_gates.rs validate_claim_ceiling_gate rejects over this exact directory: a ratchet no permitted action can retire is not a ratchet. WHAT GUARDS THIS LANE INSTEAD: an absent (lane, kind) pair is born-blocking, so the FIRST record declaring a non-canonical api_stability value reds as an unbaselined_violation at count 1; and with known_broken_lanes empty, a scan-root move reds as lane_discovery_failed or lane_discovered_nothing. There is no shrink-only count here and none is owed — the lane is at zero, not in debt.

doc-status-lifecycle._comment: 2667 docs observed. This is the repo's largest single ungoverned-status corpus and the reason this lane must be a ratchet rather than a flag day: 72% of tracked docs declare no lifecycle stage at all.

known_broken_lanes._comment: EMPTY, and the emptiness is the enforcement. An entry here is the ONLY thing that suppresses lifecycle_status_lane_discovery_failed and lifecycle_status_lane_discovered_nothing (ci/facade/lifecycle-status/src/lib.rs compare(), the `!known_broken` guards), so with nothing listed EVERY lane on disk fails closed the moment it stops seeing its corpus. The seven entries this block used to carry were never excuses to be renewed; they were a disposition question the gate made visible, and it has been answered lane by lane: capability-status, crate-status, dependency-status, feature-flag-status, migration-status and plan-status were DELETED because their declared corpus does not exist in any checkout (two of them rooted on GITIGNORED .omc agent state), and api-stability-tier was RE-ROOTED onto registry/catalog/*.yaml. The key itself is retained because parse_policy requires the object, and because adding a lane back must be a review-visible edit to a block that currently reads empty. RULES IF ONE IS EVER ADDED, unchanged: a listed lane may fail discovery or observe zero artifacts without reddening the required context; an UNLISTED lane doing either is born-blocking; a listed lane that starts observing artifacts fails with known_broken_lane_now_live and must lose its entry in the same PR; an entry naming a deleted config fails with known_broken_lane_without_config; and every entry must carry a non-empty `resolution`, which parse_policy hard-rejects otherwise. The cost of a listing is total — a lane recorded here enforces NOTHING for as long as it is listed — which is why the correct length of this block is zero.
